chunks: And said: "Have you come to us, O Moses, to drive us out of our land with your witchery?"
ai.seo_question: What did Pharaoh's people say to Moses regarding his ability to drive them out of their land?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah Taa-Haa, this verse captures the political and theological challenge posed by Pharaoh's court, who dismissed Moses' (AS) divine signs as mere sorcery to maintain their authority. Shia scholarship often highlights this as a classic example of the elite's arrogance in rejecting truth when it threatens their worldly power, a theme central to the narrative of the Israelites' exodus.
